claims.text: Under a perfectly dark sky, the peak can reach a hundred and fifty meteors an hour.
150 meteors an hour in a perfect sky

The Geminids peak in the early hours of 14 December 2026. The radiant in Gemini is highest after midnight, and the Moon sets at 20:04, so the sky is dark. Up to 150 meteors an hour is the ideal-sky rate (ZHR); from a town expect far fewer. The Moon passes Saturn on the night of 17–18 December, 5.5° at closest, and the pair is best seen on Thursday evening.

Positions computed for central Europe (50°N, 15°E) with astronomy-engine; meteor rates from the International Meteor Organization. Narration uses a synthetic voice.
